strategies.overview: In a tier lacking entry hazard removal options, Fletchinder shines as the premier Defogger, preventing teams from being weak to hazards. Fletchinder also provides a very rare Ground immunity, preventing one of the biggest threats of the tier in Choice Band Piloswine from spamming Ground-type moves. Fletchinder's great Speed and defensive typing allow it to check common physical threats such as Raboot and Thwackey and punish them with Flame Body. Fletchinder is best used on balance teams that want a good way of dealing with hazard stack teams and don't want to be blocked from removing hazards by Ghost-types. However, Fletchinder relies on Heavy-Duty Boots in order to remove Stealth Rock; thus, it needs teammates such as Koffing and Dunsparce able to come on Knock Off for it.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Eviolite can be used over Heavy-Duty Boots to provide more bulk to Fletchinder. It is an especially good option if your team has another way of removing entry hazards such as Quaxwell and Wartortle or Hattrem to deter foes from setting them up, as Fletchinder will otherwise suffer heavy damage from Stealth Rock every time it comes on the field. Since Fletchinder comes in on several Knock Off users, Thief can be used to steal a foe's Eviolite, letting it serve as a Knock Off absorber. A bulkier EV spread of 252 HP / 232 Def / 24 Spe with a Impish nature can be used to help Fletchinder check powerful wallbreakers such as Pignite and Piloswine while outspeeding Adamant Pignite. A spread of 252 HP / 136 Def / 120 Spe with a Jolly nature lets Fletchinder outspeed Fraxure to burn it with Will-O-Wisp while notably allowing it to tank Icicle Crash from Choice Band Piloswine.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Seadra, Quaxwell, and Wartortle threaten Fletchinder with Surf while being able to take the momentum with Flip Turn or get a setup opportunity with Shell Smash in Wartortle's case.

Rock-types: Fletchinder has no way of hitting Rock-types such as Glimmet and Naclstack, meaning it won't be able to effectively keep entry hazards off the field as they can both come in and set them up again.

Electric-types: Fletchinder usually does not run a Fire-type move, so Electric-types such as Pikachu, Eelektrik, and Chinchou come freely on it and threaten it with Electric-type moves—notably Volt Switch, which will give the momentum to the opponent.

Special Attackers: Due to Fletchinder usually using utility moves, special attackers such as Drakloak, Hisuian Sliggoo, and Frogadier can come in on it without risk of fainting and threaten it. Furthermore, since it's pretty passive, Fletchinder gives free opportunities to set up for special attackers such as Duosion, Girafarig, and Wartortle.

movesets.name: Utility
movesets.description:
Fletchinder's most precious tool is Defog, a very rare move in the tier. With its good Speed and defensive typing, Fletchinder is the best Defogger of the tier, as it has a good matchup against entry hazards setters like Quilladin and Piloswine while checking a lot of physical attackers such as Pignite, the aforementioned Piloswine, Scraggy, Thwackey, Raboot, and Monferno. Brave Bird hits Fighting- and Grass-types, while Roost gives Fletchinder more longevity. U-turn can be used to pivot on Pokemon that come in for free on Fletchinder such as Hisuian Sliggoo and Seadra, thus giving you the momentum. Taunt is an option to help deal with defensive walls such as Tinkatuff and Dunsparce. Will-O-Wisp hinders physical attackers such as Krokorok and Piloswine. With its ability Flame Body, Fletchinder punishes Pokemon that spam U-turn such as the aforementioned Thwackey and Raboot. The given EV spread with a Jolly nature takes advantage of Fletchinder's good Speed, letting it outspeed offensive threats such as Monferno and Servine while being bulky enough to check a plethora of Pokemon.

Fletchinder fits best on balance teams looking for a good way to deal with entry hazards. Seadra is the most common defensive teammate to Fletchinder, as Fletchinder's hazard removal lets your team drop Quaxwell for Seadra, which is bulkier, faster, and more powerful. Seadra helps deal with Pokemon that have access to Knock Off such as Pignite and Monferno, so Fletchinder can keep its much-needed Heavy-Duty Boots. Furthermore, Seadra's Ice resistance helps prevent Choice Band Piloswine from spamming Icicle Crash, while Fletchinder's Ground immunity stops it from spamming Earthquake. These two Pokemon also punish physical attackers thanks to Poison Point and Flame Body, and they can also form a solid VoltTurn defensive core with Flip Turn and U-turn. Hisuian Sliggoo is an excellent offensive partner to Fletchinder, as it is able to check Water-, Rock-, and Electric-types, which all take advantage of Fletchinder's passivity, while checking specially offensive Pokemon that threaten Fletchinder like Drakloak and Frogadier. However, other special walls such as Tinkatuff and Dunsparce are also good options, as they appreciate Fletchinder's ability to check common physical threats such as Pignite and Piloswine, while Fletchinder appreciates their ability to check common special threats such as Girafarig, Drakloak, and Frogadier. Offensive Pokemon that can't afford to hold Heavy-Duty Boots such as Choice Specs Drakloak, Monferno, and Piloswine appreciate Fletchinder's ability to remove hazards. Koffing can serve as a Knock Off absorber for Fletchinder, allowing it to keep its Heavy-Duty Boots, and Fletchinder can check Ground-types that usually take advantage of Koffing such as Krokorok and Piloswine. Glimmet being able to come in on Fletchinder and set hazards up can quickly become overwhelming for your team, so Pokemon that take advantage of it like Hisuian Sliggoo, Girafarig, and Krokorok pair well with Fletchinder. Wallbreakers like Gabite, Choice Specs Girafarig, and Choice Band Piloswine that have a hard time coming on the field appreciate Fletchinder's ability to pivot with U-turn.
